issues.t: Fuel pump can fail and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine may run rough, lose power, or stall while driving and then refuse to restart. A check engine light may come on first.
issues.why: The plastic impeller inside the low-pressure fuel pump can crack and swell until the pump stops delivering fuel. Mazda recalled affected 2019 CX-3s and other models to replace the pump.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for an open recall and book the free pump replacement. If the engine starts stumbling or stalls, pull over safely and have it towed rather than trying to restart it repeatedly.

issues.t: Mazda Connect screen freezes, reboots or ghost touches
issues.sym: The center screen picks items on its own, freezes, goes blank, keeps restarting, drops Bluetooth or navigation, or the backup camera picture does not show.
issues.why: The Mazda Connect head unit can suffer from software faults and a touchscreen that develops phantom touches as it ages. Owners filed a class action over CX-3 and other 2014-2023 Mazdas, and Mazda issued updated software and screen repair kits to dealers.
issues.next: Ask a Mazda dealer to install the latest Mazda Connect software, which fixes many freeze and reboot problems. If the screen still ghost touches, the screen unit usually needs replacing; ask about extended coverage first.

issues.t: Backup camera picture flickers or distorts (recall)
issues.sym: When you shift into reverse, the rearview camera image flickers, looks distorted, or doesn't show properly.
issues.why: Moisture and a loose wiring harness at the rear camera can disturb the video signal. Mazda recalled 2016-2021 CX-3s, along with some 2014-2018 Mazda3s, to inspect the camera, replace it if needed, and add a sealed harness fastener.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall and have the free camera repair done. Until then, use your mirrors and look over your shoulder when backing up.

issues.t: Front strut bolts can loosen and affect steering (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or knock from the front end over bumps, steering that feels loose or wanders, or in the worst case a sudden loss of steering control.
issues.why: On a small number of early CX-3s, the lower bolts that hold each front strut to the steering knuckle were not tightened to the right torque at the factory. If they work loose, the knuckle can separate from the strut.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. If the front end clunks or the steering suddenly feels loose, stop driving and have it towed to a dealer.

issues.t: Liftgate struts can corrode and let the hatch fall (recall)
issues.sym: The rear hatch won't stay up on its own or slowly drifts down after you open it. In the worst case it drops suddenly.
issues.why: The gas struts that hold the liftgate open can corrode inside and lose pressure or break. Mazda recalled 2016 CX-3s, along with several other Mazdas, to replace both struts.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. Until the struts are replaced, hold the hatch open by hand or prop it, and keep children clear of it.

issues.t: Steering feels light or makes noise when turning
issues.sym: The steering feels unusually light or a bit notchy, or you hear a clicking or grinding noise from the steering column when turning the wheel left or right.
issues.why: Mazda found that the worm gear inside the electric power steering assist unit could be made slightly out of tolerance or absorb moisture at the factory and swell. That changes how the gears mesh.
issues.next: Have a Mazda dealer check the steering under Mazda's bulletin for this problem. The repair is to the steering shaft or assist unit and is often covered if the car is still under warranty.

issues.t: Oil leak and rattle from the drive belt tensioner
issues.sym: Oily residue around the front of the engine near the belt, sometimes with a rattling or chattering noise from under the hood.
issues.why: The damper inside the automatic belt tensioner may not seal well when it works hard in hot weather and under heavy load, so it leaks oil and stops controlling the belt properly. Mazda redesigned the damper.
issues.next: Have the tensioner inspected. If it is leaking or rattling, replace it along with the belt before the belt slips or comes off.

issues.t: Broken front coil spring causes creaking over bumps
issues.sym: A creaking or groaning from a front corner when going over bumps or into driveways. Sometimes a mechanic spots a broken spring during routine service.
issues.why: Mud and sand can get trapped between the bottom of the front coil spring and its seat, wearing off the paint. The spring then rusts through and breaks near its lower end. Mazda changed the shape of the lower spring seat.
issues.next: Have the front springs inspected. A broken spring should be replaced promptly, ideally in pairs, because it can affect handling and damage the tire.

issues.t: Whining noise from the automatic transmission
issues.sym: A whine from the transmission that starts around 10 mph and gets louder as you go faster. It stays the same whether you accelerate, coast or cruise.
issues.why: A bearing inside the transmission can be damaged because of how the transmission case was shaped on earlier units. Mazda changed the design on later transmissions.
issues.next: Have a dealer confirm where the noise comes from; a worn wheel bearing can sound similar. If it is the transmission, get it repaired while it is still under powertrain warranty if possible.

issues.t: Rough idle and check engine light after a freezing night
issues.sym: On a cold morning after the car sat outside overnight below freezing, the engine idles roughly or shakes and the check engine light may come on with misfire codes.
issues.why: Water that collects in the main muffler can freeze overnight and partly block the exhaust, so the engine struggles until the ice melts.
issues.next: If it clears up once the car warms, it is likely this. If the light stays on or the engine keeps misfiring, have the codes read so a real ignition problem isn't missed.

issues.t: No-start, battery drain or odd electrical faults linked to accessories
issues.sym: The car sometimes won't start, the key isn't detected, the security light flashes, or the battery is dead after sitting.
issues.why: Mazda found that aftermarket devices such as dash cams, remote starters and plug-in insurance trackers can drain the battery or confuse the keyless and security systems.
issues.next: Unplug any add-on devices and see if the problem stops. Have the battery tested, and ask a shop to do a parasitic-drain test if the battery keeps going flat.

issues.t: Rising oil level from fuel in the oil on short trips
issues.sym: The oil on the dipstick reads higher than when it was changed, and the check engine light may later come on with a 'running rich' code.
issues.why: On direct-injection engines, some fuel slips past the piston rings into the oil when the engine is only run for very short trips and never fully warms up.
issues.next: Take the car on a longer drive regularly so the engine gets fully hot, and stick to the oil change schedule. If the level keeps rising or the light comes on, have a dealer check it.

issues.t: Forward camera fault turns off safety systems
issues.sym: Warning lights for Smart City Brake Support, lane departure warning or automatic high beams come on, and a system error message appears on the screen.
issues.why: An internal hardware fault in the forward sensing camera behind the windshield shuts those driver-assist systems off. Mazda changed how the camera was made.
issues.next: Have a dealer read the camera codes. The automatic emergency braking may not work while the light is on, so drive with extra following distance until it's repaired.

issues.t: Weak heat from a clogged heater core
issues.sym: The heater blows only lukewarm air even after the engine is fully warmed up.
issues.why: Deposits can build up inside the heater core and restrict coolant flow. Mazda raised the anti-rust additive level in its factory coolant to prevent it.
issues.next: Check the coolant level first. If it is full, have a shop check the heater core for a blockage; a flush sometimes helps, but a badly clogged core is replaced.

issues.t: Rotten egg smell from the exhaust
issues.sym: A sulfur or rotten-egg smell from the tailpipe, most often after a cold start, while idling a long time, or under hard acceleration.
issues.why: Sulfur in some gasoline reacts in the catalytic converter. Mazda says this does not mean anything is wrong with the engine and it fades as the car gains miles.
issues.next: Try a different brand of fuel. If the smell comes with a check engine light, rough running or poor power, have the car checked.

issues.t: A/C blows warm from a leaking evaporator
issues.sym: The air conditioning stops cooling and blows warm air from the vents.
issues.why: A brazed joint between the tubes and header of the A/C evaporator, which sits behind the dashboard, may not have been made properly, so refrigerant leaks out.
issues.next: Have the A/C system leak-tested. If the evaporator is leaking, ask the dealer whether it is covered under warranty, since replacing it means taking apart much of the dashboard.

issues.t: Slow warm-up and check engine light from thermostat stuck open
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, the engine takes a long time to warm up, the blue cold-engine light stays on longer than normal, and the heater is weak at idle.
issues.why: The backup thermostat built into the coolant control valve can let coolant in and open at too low a temperature, so the engine runs too cool.
issues.next: Have the codes read. If it shows a thermostat-stuck-open code, the coolant control valve is replaced. It isn't an emergency, but running cool hurts fuel economy and heat.

issues.t: Windshield cracks low in the center
issues.sym: A crack starts at the bottom center of the windshield, near the wipers, often without a clear rock strike.
issues.why: The cowl panel below the windshield presses hard on the glass at the center. Small stones caught between the cowl and glass can scratch it deeply, and the scratches grow into cracks. Mazda changed the cowl panel.
issues.next: Have the windshield replaced and ask the shop to fit the updated cowl panel. Check whether insurance glass coverage or warranty helps.

issues.t: Wheel bearing growl or hum
issues.sym: A growl, hum or whine that rises with speed and may change when you steer gently left or right. It can be mistaken for a transmission noise.
issues.why: A worn front or rear wheel bearing makes noise as it rotates. Mazda reminded technicians to check wheel bearings before blaming the transmission.
issues.next: Have a mechanic road-test and lift the car to find which wheel is noisy. Replace the bearing before it gets loose, since a badly worn one can affect braking and handling.

issues.t: Front shock knocks or squeaks on rough roads
issues.sym: A knocking or squeaking from the front suspension on rough roads, or when turning the steering wheel while stopped.
issues.why: Mazda issued a bulletin for noise coming from the front shock absorbers on early CX-3s.
issues.next: Have a dealer check the front shocks and mounts against the bulletin. It is mostly an annoyance, but worn shocks should be replaced.

issues.t: Front brakes squeal
issues.sym: A squeak or squeal when braking, and sometimes grooves on the front brake discs.
issues.why: Mazda issued a service bulletin on early CX-3s for front brake squeal and groove marks worn into the front brake discs.
issues.next: Have the brakes inspected. Updated pads and resurfaced or new rotors usually stop the noise.

issues.t: Leather steering wheel wears or peels
issues.sym: The leather on the steering wheel looks shiny, wears through or starts peeling where your hands rest.
issues.why: Mazda found the leather used on some steering wheels did not resist wear well enough.
issues.next: Ask a Mazda dealer whether the wheel can be replaced under warranty or goodwill. A steering wheel cover is a simple stopgap.
